tasks.task: Audit a page, app screen or key flow against WCAG

items.when: When a site, app or key flow needs a full audit at a chosen level with scoped samples
When you want a first automated pass on a page or code before the manual checks
When you want a second audit view with its own keyboard and screen reader test plan
When the client can only describe the product and needs likely gaps by level first
When text and background pairs need testing in light and dark themes
When the audit lists rule failures and nobody has asked who is shut out and how they cope now

tasks.task: Turn audit findings into developer tickets

items.when: When you have an audit, agency report or checker export and developers need tickets to fix and test
When a ticket must match the team's tracker fields with a clear done test
When a finding is unclear and you must go back to the rule, the user harm and the evidence

tasks.task: Fix a component for keyboard and screen reader users

items.when: When a modal, menu, tabs, accordion, select or carousel traps or loses keyboard users
When the component has no spec for its states and accessible behaviour
When the component is past patching and a clean accessible rebuild should be compared
When you have the code and want problems found, fixed and checked again in one run
When the fix must be clicked and tabbed through in a running app to prove it works

tasks.task: Make a form accessible, with clear labels and errors

items.when: When labels, groups, hints and error messages must be tied to their fields in code
When the form's fields and error messages need planning before any code
When error text blames the user or does not say what went wrong and what to do
When the form is long and a shorter field list and flow should be tried
When labels and help text use the organisation's words, not the user's
When people keep making the same mistake and the form gives no cue, feedback or way back

tasks.task: Turn an audit fix list into working code

items.when: When each finding needs a code change with keyboard and screen reader behaviour stated
When many small page-level failures can be fixed and re-checked together
While fixing, to change only what the finding needs and leave the design alone
Before the fixes are handed over, to catch repeated logic and common slips

tasks.task: Add automated accessibility checks to the tests

items.when: When the project has no browser tests and needs them installed with a sample and a CI file
When a key flow needs a test that tabs through it and checks names, roles and focus
When React components need tests for what a keyboard or screen reader user gets
When the new tests are flaky and failures must mean real bugs

tasks.task: Check new UI code before release

items.when: When only the changed screens need checking, scoped to the new flow
When you want ranked problems from the changed code before a manual pass
When the change adds motion and it must respect a reduced-motion setting
When the release touches many pages and needs a quick sweep for breakage

tasks.task: Fix colour contrast while keeping the brand

items.when: When brand colours fail and you need the closest passing colours to choose between
When the fix must become design rules, checked colours and a spec for developers
When the passing colours should be saved as tokens the whole product uses
Each month, to find drift from the rules and re-check contrast

tasks.task: Write alt text for a batch of images

items.when: When a set of photos, blog images or report graphics needs one consistent table of alt text
When you must decide if an image is decorative, functional or informative before writing
When a shop has hundreds of product photos and the text should be set on the live files
When image files also need sizes and names checked along with their alt text

tasks.task: Write long descriptions for charts and infographics

items.when: When a chart or infographic needs a short alt text and a full description of its data
When you must be sure what the chart shows, and that it does not mislead, before describing it
When the description repeats the title and should say what the chart shows and what it does not

tasks.task: Write captions, transcripts and audio description

items.when: When a video needs an audio description script that fits the gaps in the speech
When clips and a script need timed captions, a subtitle file and a fault list
When the team needs to caption and correct video in a browser themselves
When speech must be transcribed, or the description script needs a recorded voice

tasks.task: Rewrite a letter, policy or form in plain language

items.when: When a letter, notice or form is hard to read and the plain version must lose no facts
When you want a second plain version with each cut explained, to compare
When the text is an approved staff policy and needs a clear explanation beside it
Before and after the rewrite, to show how hard the text is and for which readers
When the rewrite is done, to catch slips and one thing called by two names
When the text hides who does what behind padding and vague labels

tasks.task: Make an Easy Read version with picture briefs

items.when: When people with learning disabilities need the document in short sentences with pictures
Before the Easy Read version, to get the fact list every version must keep
When picture briefs show people and must avoid stereotypes
When the draft is done, to check each sentence asks one thing of the reader

tasks.task: Write a glossary and a plain language checklist

items.when: When the team needs a one-page checklist they can use on every letter and form
When hard words keep coming back and need one agreed plain meaning each
When the team needs word lists and side-by-side examples for how to write

tasks.task: Make a PDF, Word file or slide deck accessible

items.when: When a report, form or PDF needs headings, reading order, table headers and alt text set
When a deck needs slide titles, reading order and alt text checked with exact fixes
When a finished deck will be shared and needs notes, links and a readable handout
When you need to pull the text out of a PDF to see what a screen reader would get
When a broken PDF may be better offered as a web page or Word file instead

tasks.task: Draft an honest accessibility statement

items.when: After an audit or fix round, to say what works, what does not yet and how to get help
When you need the known gaps by level set out before the statement is written
Before publishing, to check each claim of conformance can be traced to a test result

tasks.task: Review a vendor's accessibility conformance report

items.when: Before buying or renewing software, or when a public buyer asks for your own report
When several vendors must be set against a checklist to see which proofs are missing
When the buyer needs a clear pick between two vendors with points to negotiate

tasks.task: Triage an accessibility complaint or demand letter

items.when: When a customer could not use the site, or a demand letter or legal complaint arrives
When the letter makes legal claims and you need them listed with reply options for a lawyer
When the person needs a reply today that gives them another way to get the service
Before the reply goes, to check each promise and fix date is one the team can keep
When the reply defends the product and has not asked what the person wanted to do

tasks.task: Run the quarterly accessibility check

items.when: Every quarter, in the first two weeks
When last quarter's fixes must be re-checked and the statement kept current
When the same visit should also catch broken pages and other quality slips
When the check changes what is known and the public statement needs updating

tasks.task: Run an audit, fix and retest cycle to a deadline

items.when: For a launch, a redesign, a tender that names a standard, a complaint or the yearly check
At the start, and again at retest on the same sample
When findings are agreed and the fix round needs tickets
At the end, to get a go or no-go with the remaining blockers listed

tasks.task: Check against Section 508 for a public sector buyer

items.when: When a US federal buyer is involved and you need gaps, a fix plan and report notes
When one page or form needs a ranked fix list and a draft conformance note
When the buyer asks for your own conformance report and it must stand up to review

tasks.task: Check mobile app screens for accessibility

items.when: When app screens need checking for touch targets, labels, focus order and text size
When the app is for iPhone or iPad and should match Apple's own design rules
When a screen fails badly and a thumb-friendly layout should be drafted to compare

tasks.task: Review a design for barriers before it is built

items.when: When each new screen needs a ready, fix-first or rethink call before build
When one screen needs an issue list, a revised brief and a small test
When the design shows the happy path only and error, empty and loading states are missing
When the design is agreed and developers need states, focus order and names written down

tasks.task: Plan a usability test with disabled users

items.when: When you can run a one-morning test and need tasks, a script and a fix list
When a fuller study needs task scripts, moderator notes and a findings summary
Before sessions, to find blockers that would stop a participant using the prototype at all
When the test plan covers the screen and misses the everyday moments around it

always.when: When any report or statement says something passes, to trace it to a test you ran
Before any report, statement or rewrite goes out, to catch typos and mixed terms

helpers.when: When the fixes need a rebuild of pages or components in the client's framework
When accessibility checks must be built into a wider test suite and release process
When a flow is the barrier and must be redesigned, not patched
When contrast and focus fixes must be made once in shared tokens and components
When the client needs a view on which accessibility laws apply to them
When captions or audio description must be cut into the finished video

gaps: No library item writes alt text for non-product images, or checks alt text against what the image shows
No library item writes long descriptions for charts and infographics; only the kit skill covers it
No library item writes an audio description script or checks captions for accuracy, speaker names and sound cues
No library item makes an Easy Read version or briefs its pictures; only the kit skill covers it
No library item rewrites in plain language with a fact list and a reading grade before and after; only the kit prompt covers it
No library item checks or fixes PDF tags, reading order and form fields, or the heading structure of a Word file
No library item drafts an accessibility statement or reviews a vendor's conformance report
No library item triages an accessibility complaint under the ADA or the European Accessibility Act
No library item sets up automated accessibility rules in browser tests or a build pipeline
No library item gives a screen reader test script for NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver or TalkBack
No library item holds accessible patterns for single components such as dialogs, tabs and menus; only the kit skill covers it
No library item audits a native iOS or Android app with its own screen reader and settings
No library item scopes which rules apply under the European Accessibility Act or EN 301 549
No library item checks an HTML email for accessibility
